hook.text: In the 1800s, patent medicine ads promised miracle cures. Blindness, cancer, baldness—one bottle fixed it all.

buildup.text: Most 'medicines' were alcohol, opium, or cocaine. The ads were more potent than the products.

discovery.text: These ads invented emotional copywriting. Testimonials, before-and-after stories, urgency—all born here.

twist.text: The 1906 Pure Food and Drug Act killed the scam. But the copy techniques survived and are used today.

climax.text: Modern supplement ads still use the same formula. Promise transformation, cite testimonials, push urgency.

punchline.text: Snake oil died. The copy tricks it invented didn't.

quiz.question: What copywriting techniques were pioneered by patent medicine ads?
